latest.title: Biharmonic submanifolds in nonpositive space forms
latest.summary: We prove that there are no proper biharmonic submanifolds with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field in a nonpositive space form, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. We also prove that every biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in a four-dimensional nonpositive space form is minimal. These results provide substantial support for Chen's conjecture and the generalized Chen's conjecture for hyperbolic space in higher codimensions.

latest.title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
latest.summary: Abstract Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA-peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the…

latest.title: Why do some fungi grow fast and others slowly? The fungal growth-rate hypothesis
latest.summary: In general, there is a dichotomy in growth mode between ‘moulds’ (filamentous ascomycetes and mucoromycetes), and ‘mushrooms’ (filamentous basidiomycetes): mould mycelia tend to grow fast, to be short-lived and to produce asexual spores, while mushroom mycelia tend to grow slowly, are among the longest-lived organisms known and generally do not produce asexual spores. I propose that this dichotomy is due to a fundamental difference in growth strategy. On one hand, mould mycelia typically grow like a ‘pyramid-scheme’: an exponentially increasing number of hyphae provides the mycelium with a constant supply of a growth-limiting nutrient such as nitrogen. However, ‘the pyramid scheme crashes’…

latest.title: Responsible AI in Academic Research: A Systematic Review of Ethical Principles, Challenges, and Future Directions
latest.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is now present in every stage of the academic research life cycle, yet the rules governing its use remain fragmented. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review used 34 structured search strings and citation chasing to search literature published between 2015 and 2025. Guidance converges on a narrow set of standards: AI cannot be an author, material use must be disclosed, and humans remain…

Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. items.summary: arXiv:2605.13071v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are a promising framework for event-driven temporal processing. items.title: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks

items.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. However, execution feedback does not directly specify which component should change, and a locally successful revision may not remain useful across tasks or subsequent improvement cycles. Understanding how experience becomes persistent agent structure therefore requires examining when evidence justifies a change, where that change should act, and how it is…

items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
items.summary: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era of Physical AI holds a second kind of equal importance, the person augmented by AI. Alongside…

items.title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models
items.summary: Visual place recognition (VPR) localises a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images, and current foundation-model VPR models are accurate across cities, seasons and illumination, but not robust to adversarial perturbations: under a white-box attack on the ranking at an imperceptible budget of 1/255, SuperVLAD and BoQ keep at most 0.2% top-1 recall (R@1) on four benchmarks. We propose anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning (ARAFT), which fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss on each adversarial query's hardest positive and an anchor to the clean descriptor of the frozen pretrained model. Checkpoints are selected under a clean-accuracy budget fixed in advance, and the…

items.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
items.summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI…

items.title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions
items.summary: We introduce PLANTEUR, a benchmark for crop-type mapping from satellite images in the French overseas territories. Building on the PASTIS design, PLANTEUR provides georeferenced and aligned Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8 sequences with parcel-derived labels spanning six tropical regions and an 8-class label space. We define both a standard test split and a leave-one-island-out protocol to measure cross-territory generalization, and evaluate fully supervised models, linear probes, and fine-tuned foundation models. The benchmark code and data are open source and available on GitHub and Hugging Face.

items.title: Fusing Earth observation embeddings and spaceborne terrain with meteorological forcing for flood peak depth prediction from high-water marks
items.summary: Flood peak depth on normally dry land governs damage and risk to life, but is observed only sparsely, by post-event high-water mark (HWM) surveys, and depth derived from satellite flood extent is produced after the event and inherits the vertical error of the digital elevation model (DEM) it is computed from. Deep-learning flood models have in turn been trained on hydrodynamic simulations rather than on observed depths. We ask whether flood peak depth can be learned from field observations and predicted before the peak from spaceborne terrain, geospatial foundation-model embeddings and antecedent meteorological forcing. We assembled 5689 USGS HWM surveys from 39 events (2011-2025) in 24…

items.title: RoboTryOn: Synthesizing Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On
items.summary: Robot foundation models have shown remarkable performance in robot control, yet adapting them to a new task still relies heavily on teleoperated demonstrations. Egocentric human videos offer a scalable substitute, but overlaying rendered robots on human videos or retargeting human poses into robot actions leaves significant visual or action gaps for high-DoF robot embodiments. To address this limitation, we propose RoboTryOn, which treats human-to-robot translation as virtual try-on: try-on keeps the person and swaps the garment, RoboTryOn keeps the demonstrated motion and swaps the human for the robot. Specifically, RoboTryOn converts a human video into a video of the target robot…

items.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
items.summary: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures execute high-level semantic reasoning and action ex- ecution sequentially within the primary control loop, creating a fundamental tension between semantic-reasoning capability and robot agility. To address this, we propose Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes operating at independent frequencies. In ARP, a…

items.title: Beyond Foundation Models: PFN Priors Improve Tabular Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: Synthetic priors have so far served one purpose: pretraining tabular foundation models. We ask whether the same priors can improve conventional tabular models, which are trained from scratch on each dataset. We propose PriorTune, a method that meta-tunes hyperparameter configurations on synthetic tasks alone. Offline, for a given model, we fit a pool of configurations on datasets sampled from a published PFN prior and greedily select the subset with the highest winrate over the random baseline. Online, a new dataset fits only the selected configurations, so the gain comes at no extra cost. Empirically, we observe that scaling both the number of configurations and synthetic datasets has an…

items.title: High-fidelity training-free photovoltaic module mapping from multi-view UAV imagery
items.summary: High-fidelity photovoltaic (PV) module mapping requires complete instance recovery and accurate delineation. Vision foundation models offer zero-shot segmentation, but converting incomplete and inconsistent predictions across views into a complete, geometrically accurate map of individual modules remains challenging. We propose the Multi-View PV Module Mapper (MV-PVMapper), a training-free framework coupling vision foundation models with unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry. First, Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) generates candidates from original images using text prompts. Their contours are then transferred into object space through per-module slope correction to limit…

items.title: Linear perturbation theory and structure formation in a Horndeski theory of gravity without dark matter
items.summary: We study the formation and evolution of the cosmic large-scale structure (LSS) in a scalar-tensor Horndeski theory of gravity without dark matter. We impose that this theory reduces to Refracted Gravity (RG) in the weak-field limit. RG is a non-relativistic theory where the gravitational permittivity $ε(ρ)$, with $ρ$ the baryonic matter density, provides the gravitational boost required to describe both the dynamics of galaxies and galaxy clusters without dark matter. We show that $ε(ρ)$ equals the function $G_4(\varphi)$ of the scalar field $\varphi$ of our Horndeski model. The background evolution of a flat, matter-dominated, homogeneous and isotropic universe shows that $\varphi$ is…

items.title: Molecular Prior Networks
items.summary: Predicting affinity between small molecules and their protein targets remains one of the central problems in drug discovery. Due to the substantial cost of wet-lab experiments, machine learning models of drug-target affinity are usually trained on relatively small datasets, ranging from tens to hundreds of molecules. Given the inherent difficulty of generalization between different targets and chemical series, existing datasets of protein-ligand affinities are typically not used for new projects. At the same time, tabular foundation models, including Prior-data Fitted Networks, have recently shown how transformers can be used to solve machine learning problems in a single forward pass of…

items.title: The Platonic Brain: Representational Convergence in EEG Foundation Models
items.summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) predicts that artificial neural networks converge on shared representations as scale and performance increase. We test whether these predictions hold for representations of the human brain with EEG foundation models. Using EEG recordings from six participants watching a television series, together with aligned visual and language content, we tested whether EEG foundation-model representations converge within and across modalities as their embeddings become better at decoding an informative set of EEG markers. We found that EEG models with greater decodability showed stronger cross-family alignment in both local neighbourhood similarity and…

items.title: Scale-Dependent Weak-Field Dynamics in Horndeski Theory: Galaxy Rotation Curves and Turnaround Scales
items.summary: In this work, the weak-field dynamics of a gravitational-wave compatible subclass of Horndeski gravity is investigated on galactic and intergalactic scales. The analysis is performed within the weak-field approximation for stationary and approximately spherically symmetric configurations, retaining the nonlinear scalar derivative interactions responsible for scale-dependent modifications of the gravitational field. On galactic scales, the transition regime is investigated through the effective potential, the stability of circular orbits, galaxy rotation curves, and the relation between dynamical and lensing masses. The analysis shows that the scalar field modifies the orbital dynamics and…

items.title: Manifold Embedding of Deep Image Features for Image Matching via Neural Adjoint Maps
items.summary: Estimating semantic correspondences between different object instances of similar categories in real-world images is a fundamental challenge in computer vision. While the recent progress in foundation models has significantly advanced solutions for such difficult image correspondence problems, respective methods are often insufficiently regularised. For example, common nearest-neighbour matching with foundation model features often results in noisy correspondences, which is particularly prominent when solving for dense correspondences. In this work, we tackle image matching via functional maps, which have been popularised for 3D shape matching due to their powerful spectral formalism…

items.title: Mixed-Order Parity-Violating Corrections to Rotating Black Holes in Combined Scalar Gauss-Bonnet and Dynamical Chern-Simons Gravity
items.summary: We construct the leading mixed-order $\mathcal{O}(ζ_{\rm GB}ζ_{\rm CS})$ deformation of rotating black holes in a combined scalar Gauss-Bonnet and dynamical Chern-Simons effective theory, the sector in which the parity-even and parity-odd corrections act simultaneously. items.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
items.summary: Video generation has progressed from isolated clips to coherent short-form audiovisual sequences, and the bottleneck is shifting from rendering to semantic control. This report summarizes the observations and insights on multimodal understanding gained from successive generations of Kling. We argue that generation quality is the projection of multimodal understanding through the entire data--conditioning--alignment--evaluation chain, and we examine this chain module by module. Kling-MLLM, a shared multimodal foundation model that unifies image, video, audio, synchronized audio--video, and interleaved inputs, is specialized for each downstream module. items.title: TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport
items.summary: Despite their remarkable capabilities, large foundation models (LFMs) remain susceptible to adversarial manipulation. Current safety intervention methods primarily rely on the \textit{locality hypothesis}, rigidly suppressing isolated neurons or features. However, harmful semantics manifest as distributed, cross-layer circuits, rendering localized ablations both brittle against complex jailbreaks and detrimental to general utility. To bridge this gap, we propose TraceRouter++, a routing-level safety intervention framework that explicitly traces safety-relevant causal routing pathways activated under harmful inputs and realigns their unsafe activation states. Our framework operates in a…

items.title: OCR in the Foundation Model Era: From Specialist Models to Unified Models
items.summary: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is among the oldest and most widely deployed applications of artificial intelligence. This survey reviews its development, focusing on the Foundation Model Era. We define OCR through faithful transcription: within a specified visual scope, OCR should completely reconstruct the text, notation, and document structure observable in the source image, and every textual, notational, or structural element in the output must be verifiable from visual evidence in that image. We trace the development from specialist OCR models toward unified models, examining joint text detection and recognition, structured sequence generation, and the use of pretrained…

items.title: Final state of superradiant instability in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black hole
items.summary: This article examines the instability of charged black holes, using Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory and a massless charged scalar field. Our study demonstrates that these black holes become unstable in a certain range of frequencies, which causes scalar "hair" to form outside the event horizon. By using numerical integration on the coupled field equations, we show that there is a phase transition between a purely charged black hole and a hairy black hole configuration. The results show that the hairy phase appears when the temperature is less than $T_C$, the critical temperature, whereas for $T>T_C$, the system stays purely charged. items.title: GeoSim: Benchmarking Multi-Field Neural Operators for Geodynamics
items.summary: Learning reliable surrogates for geodynamic models requires benchmarks that resolve coupled fields and temporal stability. We present GeoSim, a benchmark of high-resolution two-dimensional mantle-plume simulations generated with I2VIS, comprising 237 trajectories across two parameter regimes, with six coupled fields, physical timestamps, and trajectory-level splits. GeoSim defines short-window prediction and autonomous rollout, and evaluates representative neural operators field by field. Across models, we observe a pronounced scalar--velocity gap: scalar fields are reconstructed accurately while velocity errors remain large, and short-window accuracy does not imply stable rollout. We also…

items.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
items.summary: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. items.title: Motional Decoherence of the internal state of an atom by vacuum and thermal fluctuations of a quantum field: Necessity of a fully relativistic treatment
items.summary: We consider a massive object, such as a neutral atom or an Unruh-DeWitt detector, moving at constant speed in a quantum field and investigate how motion affects the quantum coherence of its internal degrees of freedom, manifesting as quantum dispersion in the absence of a quantum field, and decoherence in its presence. Our investigation aims to serve two purposes: One is to obtain the correct results for these effects, which are essential for the design of quantum information processing schemes where the quantum coherence of an atom's internal degrees of freedom is of major concern. items.title: SPA-Q: Structure-Preserving Adaptive Post-Training Quantization for Monocular Depth Estimation
items.summary: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) has advanced rapidly with the emergence of foundation models such as Depth Anything. Their transformer-based architectures provide strong generalization across diverse scenes and domains, but also incur high computational and memory cost, making efficient deployment challenging. Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) provides an efficient and practical solution for model compression, yet low-bit PTQ remains challenging for MDE models. When applying PTQ to Depth Anything, we identify two key challenges: (i) independently minimizing the quantization error of the query and key projections fails to preserve the attention maps induced by their interaction, and (ii)…

items.title: All-For-One: Distilling Visual Foundation Models to a Fast, Memory-Efficient Visuomotor Policy
items.summary: Visual Foundation Models (VFMs) provide semantic cues such as depth and segmentation useful for robotic manipulation, but directly deploying them in closed-loop control is impractical due to high computational cost, temporal inconsistency, and distribution shift between static internet images and egocentric robot observations. We propose All-For-One (AFO), a two-stage distillation framework that leverages VFMs strictly as privileged information during training, using downstream robotic data. Following the privileged learning paradigm, AFO decouples semantic representation learning from inference-time policy execution. In the All stage, a teacher policy fuses RGB observations with outputs…

items.title: Vertex-resummed kinetic theory of dipole-symmetric bosons from 2PI effective action
items.summary: The formalism of non-equilibrium dynamics for the dipole-symmetric $U(N)$ model involving $N$-component charged scalar fields is studied on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour by a systematic $1/N$ expansion of two-particle-irreducible (2PI) effective action to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The differential equations describing non-equilibrium evolution equations of two-point functions and field expectation values related to the symmetry breaking in the dynamics are derived, which encompass scatterings between modes essential in the late-time evolution and thermalization beyond the scope of the mean field. items.title: DualEvolve: Dual-Level Self-Evolution of Mechanism and Orchestration for Recommendation
items.summary: Recommender systems are widely used in e-commerce and content platforms, where improvement requires repeated model design, training optimization, and experimental validation. Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate this development cycle. Sustained autonomous improvement requires agents to improve both recommendation models and their development workflows. However, task-performance-driven approaches select updates mainly by candidates' final scores, without a separate optimization signal for experimentation quality. We therefore present DualEvolve, a dual-level framework that co-evolves recommendation mechanisms and agent orchestration toward recursive self-improvement.…

items.title: Gauge-invariant thermodynamic description of rotating black strings in 5D minimal supergravity via Kaluza-Klein reduction
items.summary: We develop a gauge-invariant formulation of the thermodynamics of rotating black strings in five-dimensional minimal supergravity through Kaluza-Klein reduction. At the two-derivative level, we consistently reduce the bulk action and the Gibbons-Hawking-York boundary term, carefully accounting for the surface contributions induced by the Chern-Simons coupling. The resulting four-dimensional theory is $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity coupled to a single vector multiplet, with prepotential $P=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\frac{X_1^3}{X_0}$. items.title: Ramified tori and Gelfand--Kirillov dimension of mod $p$ representations
items.summary: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension of degree $n$ with $p\geq3$, and let $D$ be the non-split quaternion algebra over $K$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional admissible smooth representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(K)$ or $D^\times$ with a central character and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition has Gelfand--Kirillov dimension $n$. As a corollary, every infinite-dimensional admissible Banach representation whose locally analytic vectors have an infinitesimal character has dimension $n$, strengthening Sorgdrager's bound to an equality. items.title: TTSonic: A Unified Framework for Composable and Controllable Speech Generation
items.summary: Modern text-to-speech (TTS) systems can synthesize natural and expressive speech, yet a practical speech foundation model must go beyond naturalness to offer stable quality, precise controllability, and a broad set of composable capabilities within a unified framework. We present TTSonic, a unified speech generation model that supports zero-shot TTS, voice cloning, prosody cloning, instruction following, voice conversion, and cloning from noisy reference speech. Rather than relying on separate task-specific models, TTSonic accommodates diverse conditioning signals, including text, natural language instructions, reference speech, and text-described timbre, within the same model framework.…

items.title: Biharmonic submanifolds in nonpositive space forms
items.summary: We prove that there are no proper biharmonic submanifolds with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field in a nonpositive space form, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. We also prove that every biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in a four-dimensional nonpositive space form is minimal. items.title: LFM4Ads: Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation
items.summary: Recent work leverages large-scale pretrained foundation models (FMs) to transfer generalizable representations to downstream advertising tasks. Most existing paradigms transfer user representations (URs) and item representations (IRs), while underutilizing the user-item cross representations (CRs) generated by deeper interaction layers. Although a recent approach transfers target-aware embeddings (TAEs), it requires real-time upstream FM inference alongside downstream model inference, introducing additional engineering complexity and overhead. items.title: A comprehensive review of biosignal foundation models
items.summary: Abstract Foundation models are emerging as a promising approach to biosignal analysis, offering solutions to common challenges in learning from biosignal data, such as high variability, noise or limited annotations. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art in this rapidly advancing field. We introduce commonly used biosignal modalities (including EEG, ECG, EMG, EOG and PPG) and discuss their defining characteristics with respect to training large models. We present a structured survey of existing work across unimodal and multimodal settings covering data processing, feature extraction, model architectures, pre-training paradigms and evaluation methods. We…

items.title: The AI Is Only Human: Why a Superintelligence May Not Kill Us
items.summary: Would a machine that understands the world, and us, far better than we do have the right to decide what happens to us? This essay starts from a comparison Yuval Noah Harari made in an October 2026 interview: that we might come to stand to a superior intelligence roughly as cattle stand to us. We have occupied the farmer's side of that relation for about ten thousand years, and the view has not improved our manners. The argument it makes is small. Being better at working out consequences settles what follows from one's ends, not which ends to have. Calculative superiority alone therefore establishes no moral priority of a machine's ends over ours, and none of ours over a machine's. The…

items.title: BIOMORPHIC COMPUTING AND THE AI ENERGY CRISIS: A MATHEMATICAL FRAMEWORK FOR HARNESSING LIVING NEURONAL PROCESSORS, NEUROMORPHIC ARCHITECTURES, AND THE PATH TOWARD SUSTAINABLE SUPERINTELLIGENCE
items.summary: The El-Rakhawi Bio-Energetic Computing Framework (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23912465) pioneers sustainable AI by bridging the AI energy crisis with biological computation paradigms. Core thesis: While AI data centers consume 1-2% of global electricity (projected 8-10% by 2030), the human brain performs 10^15 operations per second using merely 20 watts. DishBrain demonstrated living neurons learning Pong with near-zero cellular energy, though macroscopic life-support systems currently require significant power. items.title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
items.summary: Abstract Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA-peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the…

items.title: Why do some fungi grow fast and others slowly? The fungal growth-rate hypothesis
items.summary: In general, there is a dichotomy in growth mode between ‘moulds’ (filamentous ascomycetes and mucoromycetes), and ‘mushrooms’ (filamentous basidiomycetes): mould mycelia tend to grow fast, to be short-lived and to produce asexual spores, while mushroom mycelia tend to grow slowly, are among the longest-lived organisms known and generally do not produce asexual spores. I propose that this dichotomy is due to a fundamental difference in growth strategy. On one hand, mould mycelia typically grow like a ‘pyramid-scheme’: an exponentially increasing number of hyphae provides the mycelium with a constant supply of a growth-limiting nutrient such as nitrogen. However, ‘the pyramid scheme crashes’…

items.title: Quality Characteristics of Plant-Based Patties Formulated with Lentinula edodes Mycelium Produced by Submerged Fermentation and Different Fat Levels
items.summary: Mushroom mycelium is gaining attention as a sustainable protein source because it can be produced reliably through submerged fermentation and has a low environmental impact. In this study, we investigated the physicochemical and sensory characteristics of plant-based (PB) patties formulated with Lentinula edodes mycelium (LM) and pork backfat at respective levels of 15/0, 10/5, 5/10, and 0/15% (w/w, wet basis), based on the total formulation weight, and compared them with pork patties. Proximate composition analysis showed that the PB patty treatments had lower fat content (0–10.68%) than the control (p 0.05). These results suggest the feasibility of developing low-fat plant-based patty…

items.title: Responsible AI in Academic Research: A Systematic Review of Ethical Principles, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is now present in every stage of the academic research life cycle, yet the rules governing its use remain fragmented. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review used 34 structured search strings and citation chasing to search literature published between 2015 and 2025. Of 359 records identified, 124 studies and documents met the inclusion criteria: 40 empirical studies, 43 conceptual analyses or commentaries, 20 policy and guidance documents, 17 reviews and 4 methodological frameworks; 83% were published from 2023 onwards. Guidance converges on a narrow set of standards: AI cannot be an author, material use must be disclosed, and humans remain…

items.title: When perfect is a warning: explanations expose shortcuts that accuracy hides in cancer gene-expression classifiers
items.summary: When the classes in a training set come from different data sources, a classifier can score near-perfectly while learning where a sample came from. We show this for cancer classifiers trained on tumours from The Cancer Genome Atlas and normal tissue from the Genotype Tissue Expression project. Six model families, including a tabular foundation model, reached an area under the curve of 1.000 yet called 80 to 97% of tumour adjacent normal tissue cancer, and 100% in an independent cohort; a few matched normal samples per tissue removed most of this shortcut. Near-perfect accuracy could not tell a shortcut from an honestly easy task, flagging 87 to 92% of models trained on such tasks. We…

items.title: Pathology foundation-model embeddings reveal a morphological landscape of breast lesions beyond diagnostic categories
items.summary: Background: Despite rapid advances in computational pathology, including foundation-model embeddings, most approaches remain classifier-based. Breast lesion pathology is an area of unmet clinicopathological need and a compelling setting for morphology-based modeling: diagnostic categories occupy overlapping morphological spectra and reflect heterogeneous pathways of tumor development, thereby posing substantial challenges for pathological diagnosis and subsequent clinical decision-making. However, approaches to delineate morphological continua across diagnostic categories and tumor development remain understudied. Here, we leveraged morphology-based foundation-model embeddings to define a…

items.title: PhenoMe: An interactive AI framework for interpretable, microscopy-driven phenotyping
items.summary: Extracting meaningful biological patterns from microscopy image datasets requires tools that quantitatively connect visual similarities and experimental context. Deep learning models, and in particular novel foundation models, have the capacity to translate images into high-dimensional embeddings that can better represent complex visual patterns. Using these complex representations analytically and linking them to experimental information, it is possible to build advanced exploratory and phenotyping capabilities. Here, we present PhenoMe, an open-source, model-agnostic framework to handle pretrained foundation model-derived image representations alongside quantitative image properties and…

items.title: Transport of Compensated Baryon-Asymmetry Domains in an Expanding Universe with Exact Spherical Diffusion and a Conditional Scalar-Field Test
items.summary: Abstract This paper examines how diffusion changes a finite, globally compensated baryon-asymmetry profile in an expanding, spatially flat Friedmann-Lema\^{i}tre-Robertson-Walker universe. Coupled baryon and antibaryon balance equations are reduced to an equation for the signed asymmetry, and the conditions for conservation of its spatial integral are stated. Using the accumulated comoving diffusivity, we derive the exact three-dimensional heat-kernel response for a spherical positive core surrounded by an oppositely signed shell whose amplitude is fixed by volume compensation. The resulting central-contrast function gives a 95\% retention threshold that depends on the shell-to-core radius…

items.title: Matter-Dilution-Triggered Recollapse and Conditional Nonsingular Cycles in a Metastable Dark-Energy Model
items.summary: Abstract Can the dilution of matter end the cosmological expansion and start a new hot phase? We study a scalar field coupled to dark matter through \(\:A\left(\varphi\:\right)=1+{\varphi\:}^{2}/2{M}^{2}\). The coupling holds a vacuum with the observed dark-energy density while the dark-matter density exceeds a critical value, and releases it into a negative vacuum once the expansion has diluted the matter. While the field is held, the homogeneous background reproduces the standard cosmological model to numerical accuracy; after the release the expansion turns around tens of billions of years later. Freezing the density seen by the field keeps all 100 coupled models of a parameter grid…

items.title: Device Stochasticity Directly Implements Bayesian Sampling in Spiking Neurons.
items.summary: Device stochasticity is considered a non-ideality in neuromorphic hardware, although stochastic neural activity supports probabilistic computation in biological systems. We show that intrinsic stochastic switching of magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) can be mapped to stochastic-threshold spiking neurons, providing a physical sampling primitive for Bayesian spiking inference. We develop a spiking Bayesian neural network (SBNN) with neuronal threshold distributions learned during training and sampled during inference. items.title: Enhanced Nonlinear Capacity of a Trapped-Ion Quantum Memristor Reservoir
items.summary: Abstract We present a numerical study of a quantum memristor (QM) reservoir based on a trapped-ion platform. The reservoir exploits nonlinear input-output mapping arising from Born-rule nonlinearity, quantum coherences, and feedback-induced fading memory to process classical time-series data.We benchmarked the performance of the QM reservoir on monomial approximation, NARMA, Mackey-Glass, and the Santa Fe time series, standard tasks in reservoir computing and quantum reservoir computing (QRC). items.title: Flexible Artificial Neurons Based on NbOx for Robust Tactile Perception in a Wide Temperature Range.
items.summary: Neuromorphic tactile sensing that emulates biological touch enables artificial systems to work with high efficiency and low energy consumption. As tactile-sensing scenarios may involve curved surfaces and different temperatures, artificial spiking afferent neurons require both flexibility and temperature robustness at the front end of artificial systems. Here, we report flexible artificial spiking neurons based on niobium oxide (NbOx) threshold-switching (TS) memristors prepared on polyimide (PI) substrates. Temperature-dependent transport analysis indicates that their temperature robustness is associated with a bulk switching pathway in the NbOx film. By integrating an oscillation…

items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.summary: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models…

Quantum gravitational mechanism for isotropization of de Sitter cosmologies
items.summary: Today, the observable cosmos exhibits a remarkable degree of isotropy and plausibly began in a nearly isotropic initial state. The properties of the Lorentzian Chern-Simons-Kodama (CSK) functional can provide an understanding of this initial state. In gravity with a positive cosmological constant, the Chern-Simons-Kodama (CSK) wavefunctional is an exact, chiral solution of the quantum gravitational constraints. We suggest that the normalizability and other issues with this functional, if interpreted as a proper state of quantum gravity, instead suggest an embedding into a larger quantum gravitational completion, and recast the CSK functional as a gravitational sphaleron with…

items.title: Multimodal training in reconfigurable brain-inspired iontronic networks.
items.summary: Inspired by the brain, we propose an iontronic physical alternative to traditional digital neural networks. We theoretically study microfluidic networks in which nodes are connected by conical electrolyte-filled channels that act as memristive iontronic synapses. Their electrical conductance is not only tunable via the channel geometry, but also depends on electrical, chemical, and mechanical signals. Leveraging this multimodal responsiveness, we demonstrate that small networks can be trained to perform nonlinear tasks. The network performs forward passes physically via ionic relaxation, while training combines this physical evolution with numerical gradient descent. We theoretically…

items.title: Breaking Local-Minimum Traps in Spiking Neural Network-Based Solvers for Constraint Satisfaction Problems via Parallel Tempering
items.summary: Abstract Spiking neural networks (SNNs) with stochastic neurons provide a biologically grounded substrate for solving constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs): connectivity encodes constraints, while spike dynamics support probabilistic search. However, fixed-temperature dynamics can trap SNN-based solvers in local minima, particularly on difficult problems. We address this limitation by integrating parallel tempering (PT) into a neural sampling solver. Multiple replicas run at different inverse temperatures, balancing exploration against concentration around low-energy configurations, and periodically exchange temperatures. items.title: Hyperbolic Hierarchical 3D Scene Representations for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation.
items.summary: Open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation aims to predict 3D objects and their predicates beyond the annotated label space. Compared to closed-set 3D scene graph generation methods, the open-vocabulary approach is more general, practical, and less dependent on labor-intensive ground truth annotations. Existing open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation methods rely on learning individual object and predicate features in the representation space while ignoring higher-level 3D scene representations, leading to overfitting and suboptimal performance. items.title: From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
items.summary: Language-model agents rely on harnesses that govern tool use, context, memory, and execution. Understanding automated harness revision requires connecting improvement methods to the reusable functionality they produce. This survey examines three linked perspectives: improvement workflows, recursive scope, and concrete modifications across task domains. We compare search strategies, memory management, edit guidance, and integration with model training, and use an existing five-level framework to distinguish harness optimization from recursive self-improvement. Across coding, reasoning and information processing, interactive and embodied tasks, and visual tasks, we trace reported changes…

items.title: AI4AI: Toward AI-Discovered Superintelligence
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how AI itself is developed. From designing learning algorithms to automating research workflows and evaluation, this expanding role has fueled the rapid growth of AI for AI (AI4AI). Yet a fundamental question remains: as AI takes on more research tasks, which decisions does it actually control? Even systems that execute entire research workflows may still rely on humans to define research goals, allowable modifications, and criteria for success. Existing taxonomies, typically organized by technique or target artifact, offer limited insight into these differences in research responsibility. This survey presents a unified, control-centered…

items.title: The Pauli Spin Algebra, Related Clifford Algebra Representation, and Derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian Operator
items.summary: I present a novel approach to derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian operator on the secondly quantized Fock space, based on the the Pauli spin \(\text{su}{(2)}\) - algebra and its Clifford algebra representation. The relativistic Lorentz invariance of the related Schrödinger equation is stated as a natural consequence of its operator structure.

items.title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Foundations Mechanisms Harnesses and Evaluation
items.summary: Embodied foundation models have expanded robot capabilities, but autonomous execution does not automatically provide autonomous improvement. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) concerns retained changes that can influence subsequent improvement, including the stronger case in which an agent revises the procedures that generate and evaluate future updates. This survey connects large-model learning and reasoning, agent memory and skills, and RSI theory. We compare general agent harnesses with embodied harnesses and organize the literature along four axes: improvement targets, update mechanisms, decision authority and evidence conditions. The method review covers reflection and knowledge…

items.title: Medical superintelligence: foundations and aspirations.
items.summary: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have stimulated discussions about medical superintelligence , yet how to define and evaluate this aspiration remains unclear. We discuss how AI technologies can contribute to more effective care, introducing six interdependent dimensions of medical intelligence to frame contributions of AI to healthcare delivery. As AI capabilities and their integration into clinical workflows advance, improving the quality of care will require more than superhuman performance on isolated tasks. It will require systems that harness AI, independently and in collaboration with humans, to surpass today's strongest human-led health systems in integrated medical…

items.title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Mechanisms Evaluation and Open Challenges
items.summary: Embodied foundation models have expanded the range of instructions, observations, and actions that robots can process. Autonomy in execution, however, does not automatically provide autonomy in improvement. Robots must still diagnose failures, acquire useful experience, select interventions, and determine whether accepted changes improve future performance. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) connects these activities through persistent feedback and inheritance, with the stronger objective of improving the mechanisms that produce subsequent improvements. items.title: The rise of super-emotional intelligence.
items.summary: The debate about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) runs along a single axis: cognitive capability and its projected culmination in superintelligence. We argue that this framing leaves a complementary axis unexamined and propose the goal of Super-Emotional Intelligence (SEI): systems that perceive, model, regulate, and respond to affect better than skilled human experts, while remaining human-centered. SEI is a performance construct realized by a functional architecture, not a claim about machine experience, and we give measurable criteria for each of its four capacities. Today's affect-aware AI, from multimodal emotion recognition to empathic chatbots, recognizes, or simulates…

items.title: Dimensional convergence at the nanoscale: a novel synthesis of experimental evidence justifying direct measurement of quantum coherence in microtubules.
